newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks fall sharply, Nikkei down 2.69%.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks fall sharply, Nikkei down 2.69%.

text.p: Tokyo stocks fell sharply on Tuesday on worries about Japan's economic prospects, with the key Nikkei index falling 2.69 percent to a fresh 12-month low.
Brokers said the market was jittery about Japan's uncertain economic outlook for 1997, despite optimistic comments from government officials about the nation's economic recovery.

The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares slid a hefty 528.75 points or 2.69 percent to close at 19,161.71. This was its lowest level since December 19, 1995, when the stock index recorded an intraday low of 19,077.12.
The drop was the third sharpest fall in the Nikkei this year. March Nikkei futures tumbled 340 points to finish the session at 19,250.

Tokyo stocks have been battered by a sell-off that took hold last week when the government confirmed it would tighten fiscal policy next year to rein in the nation's debt, with possible harmful effects on the economy.
Year-end gloom has pervaded the stock market despite assurances from government officials that Japan's tentative economic recovery remains on track.
